ROUND 9 SETTLED THE GATE FORM FROM CODE: B *= min(scale_i, scale_j) is a PER-EDGE factor, so B's direction is not preserved and Miller-MacKay's (LIT-0043) convergence theorem is inapplicable. AIEFS_salvage.md's claim that multiplicative normalisation produces the k*eta/c rates is unsupported as stated; the rate law itself is verified and not in doubt.

ROUND 9 REVERSED THE NOVELTY FRAMING: the specific prior-art models are regular - Timms & English are 1D/2D lattices with periodic BCs, Picallo & Riecke are all-to-all, Earl & Strogatz require uniform in-degree k. The residue is STRUCTURAL (irregular adaptive hypergraph with per-node caps) rather than a three-ingredient subtraction. Round 7's reading was based on titles, not models.

ROUND 9 RE-VERIFICATION POLICY: LIT-0041/0042 abstracts were read; snapshots and verification_level were deliberately left byte-identical and the new evidence was appended to notes. The frozen record is never rewritten; new evidence goes where new evidence goes. Consequence: verification_level now UNDERSTATES those two sources, which is the accepted cost.

ROUND 10 MEASURED THE GATE: 200/200 exactly proportional for global-multiplicative (sin theta 3.1e-16) vs 0/200 for the AIEF per-edge cap (11 distinct factors, median 6 degrees off). LIT-0043's convergence theorem is inapplicable, not merely misattributed. See audits/experiments/gate_form/.

ROUND 10: the rate law's derivation gap is NOT fillable by finding a better paper. The mechanism requires single-factor rescaling, which the gate provably lacks. The k*eta/c law needs its own derivation or must be restated as empirical regularity.

ROUND 10: Part B of the experiment is indicative only - 3 seeds, T_SIM 200 vs 800, all-to-all not hypergraph. The rules are distinguishable (B gap 0.60-0.73, partitions match 3/9) but NOT orderable (per-edge ranks [1,2,1]). Do not quote the mean r.

gate_form.question: Is the AIEF capacity gate multiplicative in Miller & MacKay's (LIT-0043) sense, and can their convergence theorem apply to it?
gate_form.answer: No. Global-multiplicative applies 1 factor and is exactly proportional in 200/200 trials (sin theta 3.1e-16). The AIEF per-edge cap applies 11 distinct factors and is proportional in 0/200 (median 6 degrees off). Their theorem is inapplicable.
gate_form.scope: Part A exact (property of the rescaling map). Part B indicative only: T_SIM 200 vs 800, all-to-all not hypergraph, 12-node pure-Python replica. Do not quote Part B as the AIEF attractor.
